evidence_classification: Scientific evidence: peer-reviewed review articles and meta-analyses.

sources.citation: Carpenter, S. K., Pan, S. C., & Butler, A. C. (2022). The science of effective learning with spacing and retrieval practice. Nature Reviews Psychology, 1, 496–511.
sources.supports: Spacing and retrieval practice are researched learning strategies across domains and applied educational settings.

sources.citation: Cepeda, N. J., Pashler, H., Vul, E., Wixted, J. T., & Rohrer, D. (2006). Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis. Psychological Bulletin, 132(3), 354–380.
sources.supports: Spacing and the time until desired final recall jointly affect retention; a universal best interval should not be claimed.

sources.citation: Latimier, A., Peyre, H., & Ramus, F. (2021). A meta-analytic review of the benefit of spacing out retrieval practice episodes on retention. Educational Psychology Review, 33, 959–987.
sources.supports: Spacing retrieval episodes out showed benefit relative to massed retrieval; expanding intervals are not universally superior to uniform intervals.

claim_limits: The 1, 3, 7, and 14 day sequence is a personal two-week starter experiment, not a universal optimum.
The reel makes no claim that spacing guarantees an outcome or replaces sufficient study time.
The reel distinguishes the evidence-supported practice from the chosen reminder-template implementation.
